prompt.brief: Design a predictive-maintenance platform that ingests equipment telemetry, detects anomalies, estimates remaining useful life, and creates actionable maintenance work before failures occur.
successSignals: Separate raw timestamped telemetry, equipment and sensor metadata, feature windows, model predictions, alerts, and work orders.
Use event-time windows and equipment partitions, handle missing or out-of-order readings, and preserve the evidence behind a prediction.
Turn predictions into deduplicated maintenance recommendations with operator acknowledgement and feedback loops.
Explain cold-start equipment, sensor drift, false alarms, safety escalation, offline operation, retention, and model rollback.

functional: Register equipment and sensors, ingest telemetry, calculate features, score failure risk and remaining life, and create work recommendations.
Expose equipment health, anomaly evidence, prediction confidence, model version, sensor freshness, and maintenance status.
Support acknowledgements, overrides, corrective labels, reprocessing, access control, audit history, and model evaluation.
nonFunctional: Target above 90% recall for critical failures at a declared false-alarm budget and keep health dashboards below 2 seconds p95.
Ingest 1 million sensor readings per second by equipment and site partitions without losing safety-critical alerts.
Make telemetry ingestion, feature windows, predictions, alerts, and work-order creation idempotent.
Fall back to threshold rules and last-known health when model workers or upstream telemetry are degraded.
scaleAssumptions: Monitor 1 million assets, 100 million sensors, and 1 million readings per second across sites with intermittent connectivity.
Partition by tenant, site, asset, sensor, and event time; isolate high-rate assets and incident bursts.
Retain raw telemetry, feature definitions, predictions, labels, alerts, and work-order decisions under safety policy.

dataFlow.description: Feature workers join predictive maintenance system inputs using event-time watermarks, prevent leakage, and publish the same feature contract for training and serving.

architecture.title: Predictive Maintenance System ML platform architecture
architecture.summary: Design a predictive-maintenance platform that ingests equipment telemetry, detects anomalies, estimates remaining useful life, and creates actionable maintenance work before failures occur. The design separates reproducible data and feature lineage from queued training, approved model promotion, version-pinned serving, and feedback-driven monitoring.

layers.label: ML users and application boundary
layers.description: Users and applications register data, launch runs, request predictions, and receive version and confidence metadata.

layers.label: Reproducible data and feature plane
layers.description: Immutable inputs, feature snapshots, and lineage provide point-in-time-correct training and auditability.

layers.label: Training and model lifecycle
layers.description: Queued training and evaluation produce only gated, traceable model versions.

layers.label: Inference and feedback plane
layers.description: Approved versions serve predictions and collect feedback independently from training capacity.

layers.label: Model quality and platform operations
layers.description: Quality, drift, freshness, resource, and reliability signals are visible by tenant and version.

keyPaths.label: Reproducible training path
keyPaths.description: Dataset snapshot -> point-in-time features -> queued run -> evaluation gates -> model registry.

keyPaths.label: Approved inference path
keyPaths.description: Client -> gateway -> version-pinned serving -> prediction result, with feedback returned to the lifecycle plane.

connections.label: Dataset or inference request
connections.description: Predictive Maintenance System clients submit tenant-scoped data, experiment, prediction, and feedback requests through the authenticated boundary.

connections.label: Validated data/model command
connections.description: The gateway checks identity, schema references, quotas, and idempotency before registering an asynchronous ML operation.

connections.label: Immutable dataset snapshot

connections.label: Dataset and feature metadata

connections.label: Training and data quality telemetry

connections.label: Inference and drift telemetry

deepDives.title: Reproducibility and leakage prevention
points: Pin predictive maintenance system data, feature, code, dependency, and model versions for every run.
Use point-in-time joins and quarantine failed quality or privacy checks before training.
Keep raw inputs and artifacts immutable so a result can be replayed after a dependency changes.

deepDives.title: Safe promotion and serving contracts
points: Separate predictive maintenance system model registration from deployment and require signed artifacts plus schema compatibility.
Use shadow traffic, canaries, rollback pointers, and per-version latency/error budgets.
Return model version and feature freshness so clients can explain or reproduce a prediction.

deepDives.title: Drift, feedback, and cost
points: Measure feature drift, prediction drift, label delay, and segment-level quality for predictive maintenance system rather than only aggregate accuracy.
Sample expensive inference and cap retraining concurrency with an explicit GPU or compute budget.
Keep human corrections and delayed labels linked to the original prediction and model version.

tradeoffs.title: Batch versus online features
tradeoffs.recommendation: Prefer a shared feature contract with batch backfills and a low-latency online serving path for decisions that need freshness.
tradeoffs.caution: Two independently defined transformations create training-serving skew and hard-to-debug regressions.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous versus asynchronous inference
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep interactive predictive maintenance system inference synchronous within a strict budget and queue large or expensive jobs.
tradeoffs.caution: A request path that waits for model loading, enrichment, or retraining turns downstream slowness into an outage.

tradeoffs.title: Global model versus segment models
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with one versioned model and add segment-specific models only when quality or policy evidence justifies the operational cost.
tradeoffs.caution: Many simultaneously active versions multiply monitoring, rollback, and data-lineage burden.

commonMistakes: Training predictive maintenance system on mutable data without recording a replayable dataset version.
Serving features from a different transformation or time window than the training job used.
Promoting a model on one offline metric without canary, safety, or segment-level checks.
Treating delayed labels and drift as a dashboard concern instead of a retraining input.
Allowing retries to create duplicate runs, artifacts, or promotions without idempotency keys.

followUps.question: How do you roll back a bad predictive maintenance system model?
followUps.answer: Keep immutable artifacts and a last-known-good pointer; switch traffic atomically, stop promotion, and preserve affected prediction traces for analysis.

followUps.question: How do you detect training-serving skew?
followUps.answer: Compare feature definitions and sampled values by entity and event time, expose source watermarks, and alert on divergence before quality drops.

followUps.question: What happens when labels arrive weeks later?
followUps.answer: Store prediction records with model and feature versions, join delayed labels idempotently, and compute drift or quality by cohort.
